name: A · 粗线赛璐璐
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one original 2D fantasy tower-defense enemy style audition, not a product render. Make a square concept image with exactly ONE full-body goblin laborer/grunt, front-facing chest and face looking straight into the camera, neutral grounded standing pose, weapon held down clear of silhouette, entire ears, hands, feet and axe visible. Plain single solid warm ivory background #E6DFCC, no circle, scenery, typography, labels, logo, border, glow or drop shadow. Center subject occupying about 72% of canvas height, generous empty margin on every side for subsequent image-to-video animation.
Fixed design brief across all alternatives: an ADULT nonhuman green goblin, about four heads tall, wiry shoulders and sinewy forearms, slightly bowed short legs and broad bare feet, long sideways pointed ears, a bent broad nose, small close-set squinting yellow eyes under heavy uneven brows, jutting lower jaw and two short irregular tusks. Wary, surly, weary raider expression, not smiling or screaming. Crumpled faded mustard sleeveless cloth vest, rough dark brown short trousers, rope belt with one small leather pouch, mismatched rag wrist wraps. One crude chipped iron hand axe with a short old wooden handle. Dirty hems, worn fabric, a few readable nicks, asymmetry and personality through shape and line, not excessive realistic grime. Low-ranking frontline enemy, not an armored boss. Charming in the sense of a well-drawn antagonistic game character, NEVER cute or baby-like.
Avoid oversized round infant head, huge eyes, rosy cheeks, toy proportions, smooth glossy rubber skin, 3D, CGI, Pixar animation render, photoreal, airbrushed AI concept painting, excessive bevels, realistic body horror, gore, zombies, rat anatomy, terrifying teeth, excessive filigree, intricate micro-detail. Original design; do not copy any named game's character. Maintain useful readable silhouette at small game size.
STYLE A — BOLD TRADITIONAL ANIMATION CEL DESIGN. The whole picture should look like an animator's strong ink-and-gouache character drawing scanned from paper, not polished vector clipart. Confident thick dark brown outer contour, tapered inner ink strokes, conspicuously angular cheek planes, hands and bony knees, economical small details, crisp two-tone cel shadows with broad opaque matte colored shapes. Muted olive green skin with mustard ochre and umber clothing; moderately saturated, earthy, high silhouette contrast. Squat but adult four-head anatomy, head deliberately narrow and angular rather than round. Hand-painted slight wobble in contour, a few purposeful dry edges. No hatching and no smooth gradients. Every plane visibly designed and simplified for mobile tower-defense gameplay. Make this alternative feel bold, graphic, immediately readable and hand-animated.

STYLE B — TRADITIONAL OPAQUE GOUACHE GAME SPRITE. Strongly different from a cartoon ink outline: this should look brush-painted by a human with flat hog-bristle gouache strokes, modest uneven drybrush edges and lost-and-found dark contours, large ragged color planes, only three or four paint values per material. Muted moss and khaki skin, weathered ochre vest, brown earth tones. Visible directional brush strokes on brow, cheeks, folded vest and axe head, no smoothly blended digital sculpting, no thick uniform black enclosing outline. Adult wiry anatomy, narrow slit-like eyes, broad sculptural nose, distinct bony angular limbs, readable designed silhouette. Rough humane storybook fantasy painted taste, war-weary and mischievously unpleasant rather than cuddly, mature cozy-adventure palette rather than horror. Selective worn edges, not heavy noise texture. It must feel made of actual flat paint, with no rim light, no polished fantasy illustration gloss, no 3D or vector appearance.

STYLE C — VINTAGE EUROPEAN FANTASY COMIC INK. Strongly different from the cel and gouache alternatives. Matte limited flat olive, ochre, brown and warm charcoal colors.
